  - Explanation: A capacitated residual cut covers infeasible unit regions by small endpoint and pair sets. The point-region feasibility condition is exact.
- **claim-entropy-fingerprints** (bound, [source](#stmt-gt-fingerprints)): There are families of terminal sets, respectively terminal pairs of sets, containing every such independent set, respectively every such pair $(I,J)$, with the following properties. Each coloured terminal has an infeasible coloured region as in [gt:coloured-cut](#gt:coloured-cut); in each bipartite terminal at least one of the two feasible regions in [gt:flow-cut](#gt:flow-cut) is empty. The number of terminals of either kind is $$\label{eq:transfer-terminal-count} \exp\bigl(O(N^3 2^{100gN})\bigr)=\exp(o(m)).$$ The constants may depend on the fixed palette and on $L$.
  - Explanation: A deterministic recording-and-replay procedure uses constrained entropy growth to bound fingerprint lengths and obtain a subexponential family of terminal containers.
- **claim-compact-measure-arrays** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-compact-measures)): Let $X$ be a compact metric space and $C<\infty$. The positive Borel measures on $X$ of mass at most $C$ form a compact metrizable space for convergence against continuous functions. Countable products of compact metric spaces are compact metrizable. If $\nu_j$ converges weakly to $\nu$ and $F\subseteq X$ is closed, then $\limsup_j\nu_j(F)\le\nu(F)$.
  - Explanation: Nested finite partitions and diagonal subsequences establish weak compactness for bounded measures and countable compact arrays, together with the closed-set upper bound.
- **claim-dominated-cylinder-densities** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-cylinder-densities)): Let $X$ be a compact bit-sequence space with Borel probability $m$, let $\theta$ have a probability law, and suppose $\nu_\theta$ is a measurable family of measures satisfying $0\le\nu_\theta\le m$. There is a jointly measurable $h(\theta,x)\in[0,1]$ such that, for almost every $\theta$, $\nu_\theta(A)=\int_Ah(\theta,x)\,dm(x)$ for every Borel $A$. Conditional averages of an $L^2(m)$ function on increasing finite-prefix partitions converge in $L^2(m)$.
  - Explanation: Finite-prefix conditional densities converge in the product mean-square space to jointly measurable dominated densities. Cylinder approximation also proves convergence of conditional averages.

        "exact_quote": "For every $a\\in(0,1]$ there are constants $\\beta_0(a)>0$ and $m_0(a)\\in\\mathbb N$ with the following property.       "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-lem-frame-images",
        "exact_quote": "The following statements hold for all sufficiently large $n$.*\n\n1.  *At independently sampled raw vertices and components, images of prescribed primal coefficient tuples that are independent separately at each vertex and sign are uniform subject to their individual injectivities and their prescribed same-vertex Gram matrices. For tuples using channels as well, the same assertion holds conditionally on the full self-channel Gram matrices $X_e^{\\mathsf T}Y_e$; the relevant full Gram matrix is $\\begin{psmallmatrix}E&0\\\\0&X_e^{\\mathsf T}Y_e\\end{psmallmatrix}$.*\n\n2.  *Let a fixed tuple of nominal directions use arbitrary combinations of the two endpoints’ primal and channel coefficients. Compute its rank separately in each component and sign in the *direct sum over both endpoints*, and let the total be $t$. For every preassigned $\\epsilon>0$, choosing $M_0$ sufficiently large gives, under ${\\mathsf P_0}^2$, $$\\label{eq:reference-image-cap}\n     \\mathbb P\\{\\text{all those images equal prescribed vectors}\\}\n     \\le 2^{-(1-\\epsilon)tN}\\qquad(t\\ge1).$$ This is valid for all possible ranks $t$, including $t=O(n)$, not only for bounded tuples.*\n\n3.  *The plus frame $[P,X]$ is uniform among injective maps. Conditional on it, the minus columns are independent uniforms on the affine spaces prescribed in [eq:raw-frame-law](#eq:raw-frame-law), followed only by the conditioning that $[Q,Y]$ is injective. The failure probability of this last condition, before conditioning, is at most $2^{2(d+h)-N}$ per component.*\n\n    *Given $P,Q$, the channels $X,Y$ are independent uniform-column draws on $\\ker Q^{\\mathsf T}$ and $\\ker P^{\\mathsf T}$, respectively, conditioned on $[P,X]$ and $[Q,Y]$ being injective. The two rank-failure probabilities are exponentially small in $N$. Each channel frame alone is uniform among injective maps $\\mathbb F_2^h\\to\\mathbb F_2^N$. For any fixed $q$ independent vectors in its paired ambient space, the probability that transpose evaluation on their span is not injective is at most $$\\label{eq:channel-transpose-failure}\n     2^{q-h+1}.$$ The unconditional joint channel law is bounded above by a constant, depending on $g,h$ but not on $n$, times the completely independent uniform-column law.*\n\n4.  *For $p$ independent uniform plus vectors and $q$ independent uniform minus vectors in paired copies of $\\mathbb F_2^N$, and a prescribed $p$-by-$q$ Gram matrix $G$, the probability of that Gram matrix together with individual injectivity of both frames is at most $2^{-pq}$ and at least $$\\label{eq:bounded-gram-normalization}\n     2^{-pq}(1-2^{p-N})(1-2^{p+q-N}).$$ In particular, any consistent Gram specification on a bounded number of vectors, together with injectivity on each side, has probability bounded below by a positive constant for large $N$.",

        "exact_quote": "Fix any bound $q_{\\rm test}$ on the lengths of the ambient tuples to be tested; this bound is fixed before $\\rho,M_0,n$.       "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-item-mixer-binary",
        "exact_quote": "<span id=\"lem:generic-mixers\" label=\"lem:generic-mixers\"></span> For all sufficiently large $n$ one can choose the matrices $L_j^{ef},R_j^{ef}$ and $M_a$ in [sec:geometry](#sec:geometry) so that:*\n\n1.  *<span id=\"item:mixer-unary\" label=\"item:mixer-unary\"></span> For every nonzero $x\\in\\mathcal X$ of total component rank at most $K$, every tag, label and flavor, and every fixing of the non-$Z$ base coordinates, the quadratic function $T(x,\\mathfrak a_l(s,z))$ of the $n$ remaining $Z$ bits has polar rank at least $2(J-s_0)$. It uses a space of linear forms on $Z$ of bounded dimension, independent of $n$. This space can be chosen before the non-$Z$ coordinates are fixed.*\n\n2.  *For two distinct labels and any two flavors, every nonzero parity of the indexed $L_j^{ef},R_j^{ef}$ evaluations between the two point inputs, allowing each matrix in either order or both, and optionally either or both orders of $E$, has bilinear-part rank at least $n/5$. Here a nonzero parity involving an $L$ or $R$ evaluation means that at least one such indexed ordered evaluation occurs.         "anchor": "stmt-lem-small-tables",
        "exact_quote": "The following statements hold.*\n\n1.  *For a fixed pair of leaves and a numerical small table, admissibility is the intersection of two unary orientation filters, one on each unit. Its numerical coordinate data, including injection and the bases of the effective spaces, have bounded description length apart from the nominal coefficient bases, which require $O(n)$ bits.*\n\n2.  *The key directions of the lists at either unit are jointly independent modulo its table-coordinate spaces, component by component and sign by sign.*\n\n\n3.  *Given <a href=\"#eq:recipe-scalars\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:recipe-scalars\">[eq:recipe-scalars]</a>, there is a prescription of the binary $L,R$ evaluations between distinct atoms at each endpoint, depending only on their tags, tester summaries and $p$ bits, which makes $$\\label{eq:recipe-gradients}\n     r(v_{iz})(x)=\n     \\begin{cases}\n      0,&x\\text{ is an atom of the list toward }z,\\\\\n      p_{z'}(\\widetilde x),&x\\text{ is an atom toward }z',\n     \\end{cases}$$ where $z'$ is the other endpoint of the opposite unit and $\\widetilde x$ is the matched atom there.",
        "source_id": "PM-157.2"
      },

        "exact_quote": "Suppose two units in fixed leaves have lists satisfying <a href=\"#eq:recipe-scalars\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:recipe-scalars\">[eq:recipe-scalars]</a>, the binary prescriptions yielding <a href=\"#eq:recipe-gradients\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:recipe-gradients\">[eq:recipe-gradients]</a>, equal matched keys, and an admissible injecting small table.         "anchor": "stmt-prop-collision",
        "exact_quote": "Let $\\sigma_A,\\sigma_B$ be two laws on units, possibly carrying finitely many colour or type marks. After forgetting these marks, suppose each law has density at most $2^{3000gN}$ relative to $\\pi\\otimes\\pi$. For $O\\in\\{A,B\\}$, let $\\widetilde\\sigma_O$ be a normalized restriction of $\\sigma_O$ of relative mass at least $2^{-o(N)}$, decomposed into leaves satisfying <a href=\"#eq:final-leaf-minentropy\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:final-leaf-minentropy\">[eq:final-leaf-minentropy]</a>. On each side mix the leaves with their actual masses in $\\widetilde\\sigma_O$.*\n\n\n\n*Fix a required predicate $\\Psi(A,B)$ on the marked units and an allowed leaf-pair indicator $J_n$. Use only numerical query options whose joint acceptance on an allowed leaf pair, including their separate orientation filters, implies $\\Psi(A,B)$. Suppose these accepted queries satisfy $$\\label{eq:overlap-criterion}\n \\mathbb E_{\\text{independent leaf pair}}\n       J_n(\\ell_A,\\ell_B)\\int d_A d_B\\,d\\nu_n\\ge 2^{-o(N)}.$$ Then independent draws $A\\sim\\sigma_A$, $B\\sim\\sigma_B$ satisfy $\\Psi(A,B)$ and have all four cross holes with probability at least $$\\label{eq:collision-conclusion}\n 2^{-(k_{\\max}+.03)N-o(N)}.$$ It suffices to obtain <a href=\"#eq:overlap-criterion\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:overlap-criterion\">[eq:overlap-criterion]</a> after skipping some leaf pairs, or after summing over a bounded number of numerical options. In particular, a positive subsequential overlap lower bound yields <a href=\"#eq:collision-conclusion\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:collision-conclusion\">[eq:collision-conclusion]</a> along that subsequence. With $\\sigma_A=\\sigma_B$ and $\\Psi$ the distinct-colour test, the conclusion retains that test. The statement also applies when the two sides have different prescribed law types.",

        "anchor": "stmt-lem-no-cover-rank",
        "exact_quote": "Let $r\\ge1$ be an integer, set $m_r=100r+10$ and $q_r=2^{-m_r}$, and let $s$ be a power of two with $s\\ge2^{m_r}$. Suppose $T_1,\\ldots,T_s$ are independent copies of a random tensor of total component rank at most $r$. If every fixed componentwise cover with dimension at most $rs$ in each mode has probability less than $p$, then $$\\mathbb P\\left\\{\\mathop{\\mathrm{rank}}\\left(\\sum_{j=1}^sT_j\\right)<q_rs/4\\right\\}\n \\le 4^s p^{q_rs/2}.\n \\label{eq:no-cover-rank}$$ Here rank means the sum of component ranks.",
        "source_id": "PM-157.2"
      },
      "evidence": [
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-lem-no-cover-rank",
          "exact_quote": "Let $r\\ge1$ be an integer, set $m_r=100r+10$ and $q_r=2^{-m_r}$, and let $s$ be a power of two with $s\\ge2^{m_r}$.       "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-prop-status-preparation",
        "exact_quote": "There are constants $\\delta_*,c_*>0$, fixed before the selector and channel sizes, with the following property. Along a subsequence, the original pooled unit law has a restriction of mass at least $\\delta_*$ whose first pin dimension is at most $K_1$ and whose normalized leaves satisfy [eq:final-leaf-minentropy](#eq:final-leaf-minentropy). One of the following descriptions applies.*\n\n1.  *There is no prediction as in [def:prediction](#def:prediction) on the first pooled law before the final negligible leaf trimming. For independent draws from the prepared law, the probability of an admissible injecting actual small table is greater than $.99$.*\n\n2.  *A prediction with fixed $\\alpha_i,c$ and common classes $e_i$ is retained. Its marks and exceptions are preserved, and [eq:prediction](#eq:prediction) has uniform $o(1)$ error on every retained unit. If both classes vanish, [eq:exact-prediction](#eq:exact-prediction) is exact on every unit. For independent draws from the prepared law, the probability of an admissible injecting actual table satisfying [eq:phase-compatibility](#eq:phase-compatibility) is at least $1/64$.*\n\n\n*In particular the corresponding successful pair event, measured in two draws from the original pooled law, has mass at least $c_*$. One may take $$\\delta_* = \\frac{10^{-6}\\delta_{\\mathrm{ph}}}{64},\n \\qquad c_* = \\frac{\\delta_*^2}{64},\n \\qquad 0<\\eta_{\\mathrm{col}}<\\frac{c_*}{4},\n \\label{eq:preparation-early-margins}$$ where $0<\\delta_{\\mathrm{ph}}\\le1$ is the early retained-mass constant in [thm:phase-alternative](#thm:phase-alternative). The colour bound in [eq:preparation-early-margins](#eq:preparation-early-margins) can be chosen using the initial $M$ and early geometric constants only; the marginal constant $L$ of the second distribution test does not enter it.*\n\n*After forgetting colour and other marks, the prepared law $\\sigma'$ satisfies $$\\sigma'_i\\le\\frac{M}{\\delta_*}\\pi\\quad(i=1,2),\n \\qquad\n \\sigma'\\le 2^{(D+o(1))N}{\\mathsf P_0}^2.\n \\label{eq:prepared-marginals}$$ The endpoint primal marginals consequently have the same constant bound relative to $\\operatorname{pr}_*{\\mathsf P_0}$. Every normalized leaf has joint density at most $2^{O(N)}{\\mathsf P_0}^2$. The successful table event is detected by a finite list of numerical tables and separate unary orientation flags, together with leaf-pair tests. The size of this list is fixed in $n$, but need not be early.",
        "source_id": "PM-157.2"
      },
      "evidence": [
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-prop-status-preparation",
          "exact_quote": "There are constants $\\delta_*,c_*>0$, fixed before the selector and channel sizes, with the following property. Along a subsequence, the original pooled unit law has a restriction of mass at least $\\delta_*$ whose first pin dimension is at most $K_1$ and whose normalized leaves satisfy [eq:final-leaf-minentropy](#eq:final-leaf-minentropy). One of the following descriptions applies.*\n\n1.  *There is no prediction as in [def:prediction](#def:prediction) on the first pooled law before the final negligible leaf trimming. For independent draws from the prepared law, the probability of an admissible injecting actual small table is greater than $.99$.*\n\n2.  *A prediction with fixed $\\alpha_i,c$ and common classes $e_i$ is retained. Its marks and exceptions are preserved, and [eq:prediction](#eq:prediction) has uniform $o(1)$ error on every retained unit.         "anchor": "stmt-lem-histogram-gram-normalization",
        "exact_quote": "Let $a$ plus slots and $b$ minus slots in one ambient component be independent uniform vectors, and prescribe their entire $a$ by $b$ Gram matrix.         "exact_quote": "Consider two bounded batches of prescribed nominal columns in one raw endpoint, or in two independent raw endpoints.         "exact_quote": "Fix a bounded query shape. There are constants $c_1,c_2>0$, independent of any key-space partition, with the following property. Let $A_1,\\ldots,A_\\ell$ be cells of a partition of the full slot space, with weights $w_j=\\omega_n(A_j)$. Suppose the partition has bounded size and its nonempty weights have a positive lower bound along the sequence under consideration. Conditional on any nominal inputs whose queried columns are jointly independent in every endpoint, component, and mode, the raw image probability that each query $j$ lies in $A_j$ is at most $$\\label{eq:histogram-many-query-bound}\n 2^{c_2\\ell}\\prod_{j=1}^{\\ell}w_j$$ for all sufficiently large $n$. How large $n$ must be may depend on the partition and its weight bound.         "anchor": "stmt-lem-histogram-control",
        "exact_quote": "Fix a query shape, a constant $C_L$, and an integer $F$. Consider any collection of normalized leaf laws $\\nu_L$ satisfying $$\\label{eq:histogram-leaf-cap}\n \\nu_L\\le 2^{C_LN}{\\mathsf P_0}^2.$$ The following assertions are uniform over those leaves and over the bounded numerical choices of a query.*\n\n1.  *If $A_n$ is a sequence of slot sets with $\\omega_n(A_n)\\to0$, then the probability that the unfiltered query key belongs to $A_n$, averaged on any choice of leaves, tends to zero. Equivalently, the averaged key laws are uniformly absolutely continuous in this asymptotic small-set sense.*\n\n2.  *On each leaf, choose any $F$ binary flags of the orientation and query parameters. Let $\\mathcal H_{L,n}$ be the family of unnormalized key densities obtained by filtering by any event of the orientation and the flag values. For every $\\varepsilon>0$, this family has an $L^1(\\omega_n)$ $\\varepsilon$-net of cardinality bounded independently of $n$ and of the leaf, for all sufficiently large $n$. The net itself may depend on the leaf.*\n\n3.  *Both conclusions persist after restricting the query to $\\mathcal K_n$ and expressing the subdensities relative to $\\nu_n$. In particular these subdensities are uniformly integrable: for every $\\eta>0$ there is $R<\\infty$ such that, for all sufficiently large $n$, all their tails above $R$ have integral at most $\\eta$.*\n\n*The flag functions may vary with the leaf and with $n$. The number of flags is fixed. No bound on the normalized marginal of an individual leaf is assumed here. The displayed cap concerns the orientation law after any marks are forgotten. Marks can be fixed on a leaf or included among the bounded flag data.",

        "exact_quote": "Let $F_n$ be a uniformly bounded common function of the inputs and primal keys of a fixed bounded query, with no other orientation dependence. In particular it does not inspect channel maps or the orientation’s marks. Put $$A_n(O)=\\mathbb E_z F_n(z,K(O,z)),\\qquad\n m_n=\\mathbb E_{O\\sim{\\mathsf P_0}^2,z}F_n(z,K(O,z)).$$ For every fixed $\\varepsilon>0$, under <a href=\"#eq:histogram-mixed-caps\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:histogram-mixed-caps\">[eq:histogram-mixed-caps]</a>, $$\\rho_n\\{\\lvert A_n-m_n\\rvert>\\varepsilon\\}=2^{-\\Omega(n)}.$$ Repeated labels in the query are allowed. The constants may depend on the query and $\\varepsilon$, but the estimate is uniform over tests with the given sup bound. The exceptional set may depend on the test.*\n\n*For a query at just one endpoint, its raw variance about its raw mean is $2^{-\\Omega(n)}$. This variance bound is also uniform when an arbitrary external input-and-image datum is fixed as an argument of the test. This datum may include a channel frame from a separately fixed vertex; uniformity refers to each fixed datum.",

          "exact_quote": "Write ${\\mathsf P_0}^{\\mathrm{pr}}=\\operatorname{pr}_*{\\mathsf P_0}$ for the raw single-endpoint primal law.         "exact_quote": "Fix a query template whose labels are distinct at each used endpoint. These weights may depend on the entire fixed orientation. The input laws may be conditioned separately on feasible diagonal values or tester summaries.         "anchor": "stmt-lem-unary-positivity",
        "exact_quote": "Fix an endpoint, tag, label, flavor, and feasible tester summary with diagonal $q$. For a bounded number of common global key tests, its empirical conditional key frequencies differ from $\\Omega_{l,q,n}$ by any prescribed fixed tolerance except on exponentially small mixed mass under <a href=\"#eq:histogram-mixed-caps\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:histogram-mixed-caps\">[eq:histogram-mixed-caps]</a>.*\n\n*At each unit, let $C_i\\subset\\mathcal X$ be any orientation-dependent space of dimension at most $K^2$ all of whose elements have total component rank at most $K$, and choose any basis. Fix a sequence of global single-key sets $A_n$ with $\\Omega_{l,q,n}(A_n)\\ge\\delta>0$. Except on exponentially small mixed mass, every basis assignment has, conditional on the tester summary and on $K_i\\in A_n$, fraction at least $(7/8)2^{-\\dim C_i}$. For the fixed common key sets, the exceptional event depends only on the primal frames and is chosen uniformly over all nominal profiles of the indicated rank before $C_i$ or its basis is selected. Thus these selections may depend on the channels and all orientation marks. We use the first effective spaces from <a href=\"#eq:effective-space\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:effective-space\">[eq:effective-space]</a>; the larger generality in this statement requires no further peeling.*\n\n\n*For the full generic flavor and inputs conditional just on $q$, the following conservative constant is valid: $$\\label{eq:uniform-base-fraction}\n \\beta_{\\mathrm{base}}=2^{-K^2-1}4^{-(g^2+1)}>0.$$ For every feasible specified tester summary and basis assignment, outside an exponentially small exceptional set, $$\\label{eq:histogram-base-cell-lower}\n \\mathbb P_z\\{K_i\\in A_n,\\ \\text{the specified summary and basis bits}\\mid q\\}\n \\ge\\beta_{\\mathrm{base}}\\,\\Omega_{l,q,n}(A_n).$$ In particular each joint choice of the role $a(\\operatorname{atom})$ and the basis bits has this lower bound, after choosing a compatible summary. Both roles are available for either possible generic $q$. No prescribed value of the channel flag $p_i$ is included in these lower bounds. If that bit is recorded together with the role and basis bits, the bound holds only after summing over its two values.*\n\n*The lower constants do not depend on $\\delta$, on the key tests, or on the orientation-dependent choice of $C_i$. The onset of the asymptotics and the exceptional-set constants may depend on a fixed positive lower bound $\\delta$. The exceptional set is allowed to depend on the prescribed tests: there is no simultaneous assertion over all measurable key sets at one orientation.",

        "exact_quote": "Let $W_n$ be any sequence of real functions on $\\mathcal K_n$ with $\\lVert W_n\\rVert_\\infty\\le B$, where $B$ is fixed. Extend it to the product of the single-key spaces with the same bound. For every $\\varepsilon>0$ there are constants $L,C<\\infty$, independent of $n$, and functions $$\\label{eq:weak-product-approximant}\n S_n(k_1,\\ldots,k_r)\n   =\\sum_{a=1}^{L}c_{a,n}\\prod_{j=1}^{r}f_{a,j,n}(k_j),\n \\qquad\n \\lvert c_{a,n}\\rvert\\le C,\\quad \\lvert f_{a,j,n}\\rvert\\le1,$$ with the following properties.*\n\n\n1.  *For arbitrary global unary functions $g_{j,n}$ of bound one, $$\\label{eq:weak-product-reference}\n     \\lvert \\int(W_n-S_n)\\prod_jg_{j,n}(k_j)\\,d\\nu_n\\rvert\\le\\varepsilon$$ for all sufficiently large $n$.*\n\n\n2.  *Under any mixed unit law satisfying <a href=\"#eq:histogram-mixed-caps\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:histogram-mixed-caps\">[eq:histogram-mixed-caps]</a>, outside an exponentially small exceptional set of orientations, $$\\label{eq:weak-product-actual}\n     \\sup_{\\lvert w_j\\rvert\\le1}\n     \\lvert \\mathbb E_z\\mathcal A_n(O,z)\n           (W_n-S_n)(K(O,z))\\prod_jw_j(O,z_j)\\rvert\\le\\varepsilon.$$ The unary input weights may depend on the entire fixed orientation and on any additional marks fixed with it. The exceptional set is independent of these weights. Thus one may prescribe channel flags such as $p_i$ in a unary weight without making them common key tests or asserting positivity for their individual values.*\n\n*The functions $f_{a,j,n}$ are global key functions; they can be chosen to be indicators of sets, or finite linear combinations of such indicators with uniformly bounded complexity. They do not depend on the sampled orientation. The constants may depend on $B,\\varepsilon$ and the fixed template and construction parameters, but not on $n$.*\n\n*An additional orientation-only filter of bound one may multiply <a href=\"#eq:weak-product-actual\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:weak-product-actual\">[eq:weak-product-actual]</a> without changing it. In particular, after averaging normalized leaves, the same error control applies to unnormalized admissibility-filtered query measures, even when the filter is chosen using the opposite leaf. No assertion is made for an arbitrary additional joint input filter. For distinct marked laws, use their fixed-weight mixture, with caps checked after forgetting the marks. A retained ordered type pair or different-colour condition is an orientation/leaf-pair filter, so the same conclusion applies before normalization. All leaf averages use their actual weights; no marginal hypothesis on a separately normalized colour class is needed.",

          "anchor": "eq:histogram-mixed-caps",
          "exact_quote": "Write ${\\mathsf P_0}^{\\mathrm{pr}}=\\operatorname{pr}_*{\\mathsf P_0}$ for the raw single-endpoint primal law. In the rest of the section let $\\rho_n$ be a law on units satisfying, after forgetting any finite marks, for a fixed $C$ and some $a_n\\to0$, $$\\label{eq:histogram-mixed-caps}\n \\rho_n\\le2^{CN}{\\mathsf P_0}^2,\n \\qquad \\operatorname{pr}_*(\\rho_n)_i\n       \\le M2^{a_nN}{\\mathsf P_0}^{\\mathrm{pr}}\\quad(i=1,2).$$ Changing the fixed factor $M$ does not matter. Since $M_0$ is fixed, $a_nN=o(n)$. The law may have arbitrary dependence between its two endpoints. A decomposition into leaves does not change <a href=\"#eq:histogram-mixed-caps\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:histogram-mixed-caps\">[eq:histogram-mixed-caps]</a> for its mixture. The second inequality is solely a primal marginal bound. No $M2^{o(N)}{\\mathsf P_0}$ bound on the full endpoint law is required or asserted. In particular $\\operatorname{pr}_*\\pi={\\mathsf P_0}^{\\mathrm{pr}}$ allows endpoint caps relative to the thinned law $\\pi$ to supply this hypothesis. Projecting the first inequality also gives $\\operatorname{pr}_*\\rho_n\\le2^{CN}({\\mathsf P_0}^{\\mathrm{pr}})^2$.",
          "source_id": "PM-157.2"
        }

        "anchor": "stmt-lem-limit-global-projection",
        "exact_quote": "Let $(K_n,\\nu_n)$ be finite probability spaces. On each first-side leaf $L$ and each second-side leaf $L'$ let there be a family of subdensities. Assume that, for each fixed $R<\\infty$ and $\\varepsilon>0$, their truncations at height $R$ have $L^1(\\nu_n)$ nets of uniformly bounded size, with the nets chosen using their own leaf only. The bounds may depend on $R,\\varepsilon$ but not on $n$ or the leaf.*\n\n\n*For every $R<\\infty$ and $\\eta>0$, there are deterministic partitions $\\mathcal P_n$ of uniformly bounded size such that the following holds. These partitions may depend on the leaf laws, but are chosen before the leaves are sampled. For independent leaves, choose a member $f$ and a member $g$ of the two truncated families, allowing either choice to depend on both leaves. If $P_n$ is conditional expectation onto $\\mathcal P_n$, then $$\\label{eq:limit-projection-error}\n\\mathbb E\\bigl|\\langle f,g\\rangle-\\langle P_nf,P_ng\\rangle\\bigr|\\le\\eta.$$ The same conclusion holds for every deterministic refinement of $\\mathcal P_n$ chosen independently of the sampled leaves. Multiplication of the discrepancy by any indicator determined by the leaf pair does not increase the bound.",
        "source_id": "PM-157.2"
      },
      "evidence": [
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-lem-limit-global-projection",
          "exact_quote": "Let $(K_n,\\nu_n)$ be finite probability spaces. On each first-side leaf $L$ and each second-side leaf $L'$ let there be a family of subdensities. Assume that, for each fixed $R<\\infty$ and $\\varepsilon>0$, their truncations at height $R$ have $L^1(\\nu_n)$ nets of uniformly bounded size, with the nets chosen using their own leaf only. The bounds may depend on $R,\\varepsilon$ but not on $n$ or the leaf.*\n\n\n*For every $R<\\infty$ and $\\eta>0$, there are deterministic partitions $\\mathcal P_n$ of uniformly bounded size such that the following holds. These partitions may depend on the leaf laws, but are chosen before the leaves are sampled. For independent leaves, choose a member $f$ and a member $g$ of the two truncated families, allowing either choice to depend on both leaves. If $P_n$ is conditional expectation onto $\\mathcal P_n$, then $$\\label{eq:limit-projection-error}\n\\mathbb E\\bigl|\\langle f,g\\rangle-\\langle P_nf,P_ng\\rangle\\bigr|\\le\\eta.$$ The same conclusion holds for every deterministic refinement of $\\mathcal P_n$ chosen independently of the sampled leaves. Multiplication of the discrepancy by any indicator determined by the leaf pair does not increase the bound.",
          "source_id": "PM-157.2"
        }

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-lem-limit-model",
        "exact_quote": "There is a subsequence and a common limiting experiment with the following properties.*\n\n1.  *For each tag and diagonal bit $(l,q)$ there is a compact bit-sequence space $\\Xi_{l,q}$ with reference law $m_{l,q}$. For each key shape there is a compact tuple-test space $\\Upsilon$ with reference law $\\rho$. Here $\\rho$ denotes this measure, distinct from the scalar thinning parameter in [lem:channel-thinning](#lem:channel-thinning). Its single-position projections $\\xi_\\ell$ have the independent laws $m_{l_\\ell,q_\\ell}$.*\n\n\n2.  *A base orientation array $\\theta$ contains its bounded discrete metadata and its single-atom status measures. For a unary type $t=(i,l,s,\\varphi,q)$ and a full numerical status $\\upsilon$, these measures have jointly measurable densities $$\\label{eq:limit-unary-densities}\n    h^\\theta_{t,\\upsilon}:\\Xi_{l,q}\\longrightarrow[0,1],\\qquad\n    \\sum_\\upsilon h^\\theta_{t,\\upsilon}=1\\quad m_{l,q}\\text{-almost everywhere}.$$ For the full generic flavor, the sum of these densities over statuses with any specified role and basis vector in the recorded actual dimension is bounded below by a positive construction constant, almost everywhere. Compatible finer tester requirements have the lower fractions supplied by [lem:unary-positivity](#lem:unary-positivity).*\n\n3.  *There is first a random limiting leaf-pair record $Z$, which includes two conditional laws $\\Lambda_A,\\Lambda_B$ of the arrays and their finite flag vectors. Conditional on $Z$, the two orientation records are drawn independently from these laws. After flags are dropped and $Z$ is averaged out, $\\theta_A,\\theta_B$ are independent with their respective base laws; they are identically distributed when the two original laws coincide. The record also includes the limiting permitted-pair bit $J(Z)$.*\n\n4.  *Every discrete assertion of table usability, injection, and any imposed phase compatibility is retained, jointly with $J$ and with its probability. Thus the preparation guarantees from [prop:status-preparation](#prop:status-preparation), when imposed, remain valid in this experiment: the no-prediction branch has a passed injecting table on mass at least $.99$, and the predicted branch has the stated positive mass of passed compatible injecting tables. Each imposed prediction whose error tends to zero is exact in the limiting status measures outside its stored exceptions. No prediction is required for the construction of the model itself.*\n\n*All single-key tests used to define $\\Xi_{l,q}$ are functions of global keys only.",
        "source_id": "PM-157.2"
      },

<a id="pm-s2"></a>
## 2. Definitions, validity and bounds

- **Well-signed matrix** ([source](#pm-h-3)): A real symmetric matrix $M$, indexed by the vertices of a finite nonempty simple graph $G=(V,E)$, is *well-signed for $G$* if, for distinct vertices $u,v$, $$M_{uv}<0\quad\text{when }\{u,v\}\in E,\qquad M_{uv}=0\quad\text{when }\{u,v\}\notin E.$$
- **Strong Arnold Property** ([source](#pm-h-3)): Such a matrix has the *Strong Arnold Property* if the only real symmetric matrix $X$ satisfying $$MX=0,\qquad X_{uu}=0\ (u\in V),\qquad X_{uv}=0\ (\{u,v\}\in E)$$ is $X=0$.
- **Colin de Verdière invariant** ([source](#pm-h-3)): The Colin de Verdière invariant is $$\mu(G)=\max\left\{\dim\ker M:\ \begin{array}{l} M\text{ is well-signed for }G,\quad n_-(M)=1,\\ M\text{ has the Strong Arnold Property} \end{array}\right\},$$ where $n_-(M)$ counts negative eigenvalues with multiplicity.
- **Independence number and chromatic number** ([source](#pm-h-3)): Write $\alpha(G)$ and $\chi(G)$ for the independence number and chromatic number.
- **Hadwiger number** ([source](#pm-h-4)): Write $h(G)$ for the largest $t$ such that $K_t$ is a minor of $G$.
- **Graph hole** ([source](#pm-h-5)): A *hole* of a graph is a pair of distinct nonadjacent vertices.
- **Conflicting edges** ([source](#pm-h-5)): Two edges *conflict* if they are disjoint and all four cross pairs between their endpoints are holes.
- **Edge–point conflict** ([source](#pm-h-5)): An edge and a vertex conflict if the vertex is distinct from both endpoints and both cross pairs are holes.
- **Touching edges** ([source](#pm-h-5)): Edges *touch* if they have a common endpoint or an edge joins their endpoint sets.
- **Fractional colouring** ([source](#pm-h-5)): A fractional colouring assigns nonnegative real weights $w_I$ to these sets with $\sum_{I\ni v}w_I\ge1$ at every vertex $v$.
- **Ordinary fractional chromatic number** ([source](#pm-h-5)): The ordinary fractional chromatic number $\chi_f(G)$ is the minimum of $\sum_Iw_I$ over all such assignments.
- **List chromatic number** ([source](#pm-h-5)): The list chromatic number $\chi_{\mathrm{list}}(G)$ is the least integer $k$ such that every assignment of finite colour lists of size at least $k$ to the vertices admits a proper colouring from those lists.
- **Lorentz space** ([source](#pm-h-8)): A *Lorentz space* is a finite-dimensional real vector space with bilinear form $$[x,y]=-x_0y_0+\sum_{j=1}^d x_jy_j.$$
- **Future unit hyperboloid** ([source](#pm-h-8)): Its future unit hyperboloid is $$\mathbb H^d=\{x:[x,x]=-1,\ x_0>0\}, \qquad d_{\mathbb H}(x,y)=\operatorname{arcosh}(-[x,y]).$$
- **Positive Lorentz subspace** ([source](#mt:hyperbolic-segment)): A subspace $P$ is *positive* if the Lorentz form restricted to it is positive definite.
- **Flat associated with a positive subspace** ([source](#mt:hyperbolic-segment)): Its associated *flat* is $$F_P=P^\perp\cap\mathbb H^d.$$
- **Finite metric tree** ([source](#pm-h-9)): A *finite metric tree* is a finite tree whose edges are intervals of positive lengths, equipped with path distance; a single point is also allowed.
- **Loads at most one** ([source](#mt:loads)): An edge family $\mathcal E\subseteq E(G)$ has *loads at most one* if its nonnegative weights satisfy $$\label{mt:loads} \sum_{e\in\mathcal E:\,v\in e}w_e\le1 \qquad(v\in V(G)).$$
- **Cut-profile space and representation** ([source](#pm-h-18)): The cut-profile space is $$\label{eq:cut-profile-space} \mathcal X= \left\{x=(x_{\{l,l'\}})_{\{l,l'\}\in\mathcal E}: x_{\{l,l'\}}=w_l+w_{l'},\quad w_l\in W_l\right\}.$$
- **Algebraic hole relation** ([source](#stmt-def-hole)): Two raw vertices $i,j$ have a *hole* between them if there exist $\lambda_i,\lambda_j\in\mathcal X$ such that $$\label{eq:hole-equations} \begin{gathered} U_i\lambda_i=U_j\lambda_j,\qquad u_jU_i=r(\lambda_i),\qquad u_iU_j=r(\lambda_j),\\ a(\lambda_i)+a(\lambda_j)=1. \end{gathered}$$ The middle two identities are identities of linear functionals on the whole cut-profile space.
- **Unit** ([source](#sec:distributions)): A *unit* is an ordered pair of raw vertices with no hole between its endpoints.
- **Pin space** ([source](#pm-h-25)): A *pin space* is a specified subspace $D_{O,e}^\pm$ of this nominal direct sum together with specified exact images of every vector in a chosen basis.
- **Rank modulo the pins** ([source](#pm-h-25)): For a tested tuple of directions, its *rank modulo the pins* is the sum, over components and signs, of the dimensions of the spans of its images in the quotients by $D_{O,e}^\pm$.
- **Atoms and flavors** ([source](#stmt-def-atom)): For a tag $l$, selector $s$, and base point $z$ allowed at $l$, let $\mathfrak a_l(s,z)\in\mathcal X$ be the cut profile represented by $w_l=v(s,z)v(s,z)^{\mathsf T}$ and $w_t=0$ for $t\ne l$. Its diagonal bit is $q=\eta(w_l)$ and its role bit is $a(\mathfrak a_l(s,z))$. A generic flavor retains all base coordinates allowed at $l$. A shared-only flavor sets all $O$ blocks to zero. A pure flavor sets $S$ to zero and retains a specified subset of the allowed $O$ blocks, setting the others to zero. Every flavor retains both $\#$ and $Z$ in their entirety. At a fixed label, a parameter test samples all retained bits independently and uniformly. Its tester summary is the list of all individual quadratic tester values. In addition to this summary we may record the basis values of $T(\mathfrak a_l(s,z),\cdot)\|_{C_i}$.
- **Small table** ([source](#stmt-def-small-table)): For a leaf and component, put $$\mathcal J_{O,e}^{\pm} =\bigoplus_{i\in O}(S_{i,e}^{\pm}\oplus H_i^{\pm}).$$ For two leaves belonging to units $A,B$, a small table specifies the two cross bilinear forms on $\mathcal J_{A,e}^+\times\mathcal J_{B,e}^-$ and $\mathcal J_{B,e}^+\times\mathcal J_{A,e}^-$, for every $e$. It is admissible for two orientations if it agrees with their actual cross Grams whenever at least one of the two table arguments is a stored pin direction. Let $H_{i,0}^{\pm}$ be the projection of the appropriate pin space onto $H_i^{\pm}$, and fix a complement $H_i^{\pm}=H_{i,0}^{\pm}\oplus H_{i,1}^{\pm}$. The complement is called private. We identify the two channel coordinate copies with $\mathbb F_2^h$ in their common column order. The table is injecting if, for each component, each orientation of the roles $O,O'$, and $i\in O,z\in O'$, the following maps are injective: $$\begin{aligned} \label{eq:table-injection} D_{O,e}^+\cap\mathcal B_i&\longrightarrow\mathbb F_2^h/H_{z,0}^+, &d&\longmapsto\text{table evaluation of $d$ against $Y_z$},\\ D_{O,e}^-\cap\mathcal B_i&\longrightarrow\mathbb F_2^h/H_{z,0}^-, &d&\longmapsto\text{table evaluation of $d$ against $X_z$}. \notag \end{aligned}$$ These quotient conditions use the standard coordinate dot pairing on the channels. For instance, the first image is zero in the quotient precisely when it pairs to zero with all vectors annihilating $H_{z,0}^+$.
- **Componentwise cover** ([source](#stmt-auto-definition-1)): A componentwise cover is a collection of subspaces $T_e^\pm\subseteq V_e^\pm$. A tensor $\xi=(\xi_e)_e$ is covered by it if $$\xi_e\in T_e^+\otimes V_e^-+V_e^+\otimes T_e^- \quad\text{for every }e.$$ The dimensions of the two modes of the cover are $\sum_e\dim T_e^+$ and $\sum_e\dim T_e^-$.
- **Common prediction** ([source](#stmt-def-prediction)): A prediction along a subsequence consists of common binary functions $$f_{i,n}(l,q,\cdot):\Omega_{l,q,n}\longrightarrow\mathbb F_2, \qquad i=1,2,$$ a set of units of mass at least $10^{-6}$, and, on every unit in this set, choices $$\lambda_i\in C_i^{\mathrm{old}},\qquad \alpha_i\in\mathbb F_2,\qquad {\cal E}_i\subseteq\mathbb F_2^b,\quad \|{\cal E}_i\|\le B_*,$$ such that the following uniform statement holds. There is $\varepsilon_n\to0$ for which, at both endpoints, at every label outside ${\cal E}_i$, at every tag, and in every permitted flavor, a uniform parameter atom $x$ satisfies $$p_i(x)=T(\lambda_i,x)+\alpha_i a(x) +f_{i,n}(l,q,\operatorname{key}(x)) \label{eq:prediction}$$ except with probability at most $\varepsilon_n$. Here $p_i=u_{i'}U_i$, where $i'$ is the other endpoint. The functions $f_{i,n}$ are the same for all retained units. The marks $\lambda_i,\alpha_i,{\cal E}_i$ may depend on the whole unit.
- **Numerical option** ([source](#stmt-def-limit-option)): A numerical option specifies a recipe shape with between one and seven positions on each cross edge, together with the following data: 1. the endpoint, tag, label, flavor, and diagonal bit at every position; 2. the full numerical unary statuses required at those positions, including the tester summary, the role $a(\mathrm{atom})$, the basis coordinates of $T(\mathrm{atom},\cdot)\|_{C_i}$, and the $p_i$ bit; 3. the required within-endpoint binary evaluations, and the off-position Gram conditions defining the reference key space; 4. the small tables and the finite coordinate formats in which they are written. The two sides have matching tags and diagonal bits position by position. All labels used at one endpoint are distinct. Coordinate formats of smaller dimension are padded by zeros.
- **Available generator** ([source](#stmt-def-status-generator)): On the cross edge $(i,j)$, a vector $$\label{eq:status-generator-vector} g=(q,h_{A,i},h_{B,j},\mathbf x_{A,i},\mathbf x_{B,j},p_{A,i},p_{B,j})$$ is an available generator if some common tag, surviving label at each end, and allowed flavors give positive overlap as in <a href="#eq:limit-positive-generator" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:limit-positive-generator">[eq:limit-positive-generator]</a> for these entries. Entries of the tester summary not displayed in <a href="#eq:status-generator-vector" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:status-generator-vector">[eq:status-generator-vector]</a> are summed over. A generator is retained with one such certificate of its tags, labels, and flavors. Let $V_{ij}$ be the binary span of these generators. Its *base projection* forgets the final two $p$ entries and has target $$B_{ij}=\mathbb F_2\oplus\mathbb F_2\oplus\mathbb F_2\oplus \mathbb F_2^{\dim C_{A,i}}\oplus\mathbb F_2^{\dim C_{B,j}}.$$
- **Twisted cut norm** ([source](#sec:product-tests)): For a real function $D$ on the keys of $I\cup J$, define its twisted cut norm by $$\label{eq:twisted-cut-norm} \lVert D\rVert_{\square,\mathcal T} =\max_{\tau\in\mathcal T_{I,J}} \sup_{\lvert f\rvert,\lvert g\rvert\le1} \lvert \int D(k_I,k_J)\tau(k_I,k_J)f(k_I)g(k_J) \,d\overline\Omega_{I\cup J,n}\rvert.$$
- **Relative entropy in the finite graph transfer** ([source](#pm-h-83)): For probabilities $p,q$ on a finite space with $q>0$, define $$\mathsf D(p\Vert q)=\sum_xp(x)\log\frac{p(x)}{q(x)}, \qquad 0\log0=0.$$

| q-fractional-colouring-lower-bound | \chi_f(G) | ≥ | $\frac{\|V(G)\|}{\alpha(G)}$ | The estimate applies to each finite nonempty simple graph. |
| q-linear-list-bound | \chi_{\mathrm{list}}(G) | ≤ | $C\bigl(\mu(G)+1\bigr)$ | The absolute integer is imported from the companion list-colouring theorem. |
| q-flat-gram-operator-bound | \\|[A,A]\\|_{\mathrm{op}} | ≤ | $k(\cosh^2R+\sinh^2R)$ | The bound depends on the block count and common radius, independently of subspace dimensions. |
| q-tree-additive-error | K(\ell) | = | $4+2\log\bigl(\max\{1,\ell-1\}\bigr)$ | The marked-point count is positive; logarithms in this estimate are natural. |
| q-segment-lift-error | \bigl\|d_{\mathbb H}(\widehat p,\widehat q)-d_T(p,q)\bigr\| | ≤ | $11K(\ell+2)$ | Degenerate segments are included. |
| q-load-matching-size | matching size | ≥ | $W/2$ | The total edge weight is the parameter in the matching lower bound. |
| q-matrix-rank-obstruction | \mathop{\mathrm{rank}}M | > | $\frac{ms}{2}+1$ | The base graph and graph parameters are fixed before the blow-up parameter grows. |
| q-spectral-involution-error | \limsup_j\frac{\\|B_j^2-I\\|_{\mathrm F}^2}{v_j} | ≤ | $2\delta$ | The operator bound is fixed before taking the limit and does not enter the resulting constant. |
| q-rounding-omitted-coordinates | \#\{\text{omitted coordinates}\} | ≤ | $5\tau^2v$ | The error parameter obeys the smallness hypothesis of the matching lemma. |
| q-rounding-frobenius-error | \\|B-W\\|_{\mathrm F}^2 | ≤ | $8\tau^2v$ | The stated dimension and small-error hypotheses apply. |
| q-trace-cross-frobenius-bound | \limsup_j\frac{\\|\langle H_j,Q_j\rangle\\|_{\mathrm F}^2}{v_j} | ≤ | $2\eta$ | The conclusion is independent of the fixed joint operator bound. |
| q-thinned-law-density | \pi^2 | ≤ | $2^{\varepsilon_{\rm ch}N}{\mathsf P_0}^2$ | Channel dimension precedes the thinning rate, which precedes the ambient dimension multiplier. |
| q-leaf-image-freshness | probability of a specified exact-image constraint | ≤ | $2^{-(1-\zeta)tN}$ | The tested rank is positive; leaves retain their actual mixture weights. |
| q-restricted-leaf-image-freshness | probability of a specified exact-image constraint after restriction | ≤ | $2^{-(1-2\zeta)tN}$ | The original pins remain fixed and the rank is positive. |
| q-effective-space-dimension | \dim C_i | ≤ | $K^2$ | The conservative pin budget is fixed before selector and channel choices. |
| q-gradient-tested-entries | number of prescribed primal-versus-channel entries | ≤ | $16\|\mathcal E\|h\dim\mathcal B$ | The coefficient of the linear input-dimension count is fixed before the final dimension multiplier. |
| q-key-slot-budget | k | ≤ | $56(g-1)$ | Slots count components and signs over the bounded atom lists. |
| q-filtered-collision-probability | probability of the required predicate and all cross holes | ≥ | $2^{-(k_{\max}+.03)N-o(N)}$ | Leaf restrictions have subexponential reciprocal mass and actual leaf weights are used. |
| q-distribution-conflict-probability | \Pr(A\bowtie z) | ≥ | $2^{-100gN}$ | The endpoint-density constant is fixed before selector and channel parameters. |
| q-fresh-generator-list-length | available generators per edge | ≤ | $7$ | Lists are nonempty and endpoint labels remain distinct across incident lists. |
| q-terminal-family-count | number of terminals | = | $\exp\bigl(O(N^3 2^{100gN})\bigr)$ | The palette and endpoint-density constant are fixed; the count is subexponential in the sample order. |
| q-sampled-base-order | m | = | $2^{1000gN}$ | All construction constants are fixed before the unbounded input dimension. |

<a id="pm-s3"></a>
## 3. Proof roadmap

- **step-flat-normalization** [claim](#stmt-mt-flat-normalization) / [proof](#proof-stmt-mt-flat-normalization): Use Lorentz orthogonal projection and coordinates about a common future unit point. -> Dimension-independent joint Gram control near a common flat neighbourhood.
- **step-tree-approximation** [claim](#stmt-mt-finite-metric) / [proof](#proof-stmt-mt-finite-metric): Close radial common-depth estimates under maximum–minimum chains and form a rooted metric tree. -> Marked tree distances with logarithmic additive error.
- **step-segment-lifting** [claim](#stmt-mt-segment-comparison) / [proof](#proof-stmt-mt-segment-comparison): Apply exact tree segment identities to an enlarged marked configuration. -> Uniform distance comparison for lifted segment points.
- **step-fixed-tree-bags** [claim](#stmt-mt-finite-tree) / [proof](#proof-stmt-mt-finite-tree): Thicken flat-representative hulls, bound bag radii, and select a constant finite combinatorial pattern along a subsequence. -> Intersecting subtrees with uniformly bounded normalized Gram bags.
- **step-load-and-bag-extraction** [claim](#stmt-mt-common-bag) / [proof](#proof-stmt-mt-common-bag): Extract matchings from loads, find a vertex sink and weighted centroid bag, and compare cumulative label absence along their connecting path. -> A common bag retaining nearly all vertex labels and positive candidate edge weight.
- **step-positive-blocks-and-spectral-support** [claim](#stmt-mr-spectral-support) / [proof](#proof-stmt-mr-spectral-support): Combine inverse-root positivity with spectral moments, inertia, weak compactness, and rank-nullity. -> Sign-preserving normalization and an absolute normalized involution-error bound.
- **step-coordinate-pair-rounding** [claim](#stmt-mr-matching) / [proof](#proof-stmt-mr-matching): Retain mutual dominant entries of good rows and bound omitted row mass by the involution error. -> An approximate coordinate matching with explicit omission and Frobenius bounds.
- **step-cross-trace-bound** [claim](#stmt-mr-trace-cross) / [proof](#proof-stmt-mr-trace-cross): Remove the bounded negative part and apply a positive-semidefinite spectral cutoff. -> An absolute normalized cross-Gram bound.
- **step-matrix-rank-contradiction** [claim](#stmt-thm-matrix-obstruction) / [proof](#proof-stmt-mr-trace-cross-2): Normalize clique blocks, round coordinate pairs, select candidate groups in a common bag, normalize again, and add exact complementary positive directions. -> A positive rank gap contradicting the hypothetical low-rank sequence.
- **step-cut-kernel-and-hole-parity** [claim](#stmt-lem-hole-triangle-free) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-hole-triangle-free): Identify the constant cut-map kernel and sum the gradient identities around a proposed hole triangle. -> A symmetric loopless triangle-free hole relation.
- **step-reference-frame-counts** [claim](#stmt-lem-frame-images) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-frame-images): Extend paired-frame isomorphisms to ambient automorphisms and count independent columns with prescribed evaluations. -> Uniform restricted-image laws and rank-sensitive prescribed-image bounds.
- **step-channel-thinning** [claim](#stmt-lem-channel-thinning) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-channel-thinning): Choose sparse random image subsets and prove simultaneous concentration of survival, fixed transpose-test, and translated-event numerators. -> A thinned law with unchanged primal marginal and suppressed translated channel hits.
- **step-intersections-and-peeling** [claim](#stmt-lem-peeling) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-peeling): Exclude large primal intersections, condition on violating image constraints, and charge each positive rank increment to the absolute density budget. -> Sparse true-intersection profiles and leaves with bounded exact pins and image freshness.
- **step-walsh-estimates** [claim](#stmt-lem-walsh) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-walsh): Use orthogonality of the binary dot-product character matrix and rank reduction. -> Rank-dependent bilinear correlation bounds.
- **step-low-rank-moment-labels** [claim](#stmt-lem-sparse-pin-labels) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-sparse-pin-labels): Characterize Boolean base moments, build commuting selector-coordinate idempotents on a flat quotient, and compare sparse representations using selector interpolation. -> Low-rank label decompositions and a bounded forbidden-label set at each endpoint.
- **step-high-rank-mixers** [claim](#stmt-item-mixer-binary) / [proof](#proof-stmt-item-mixer-binary): Count low-rank profiles and exclude bad random matrix restrictions by union bounds. -> Fixed mixers with uniform unary polar-rank and distinct-label binary-rank guarantees.
- **step-small-tables** [claim](#stmt-lem-small-tables) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-small-tables): Separate admissibility by pinned arguments, prove fresh key independence, and extend consistent row-sum data to a symmetric binary form. -> Unary table flags and consistent within-endpoint binary prescriptions.
- **step-gradient-realization** [claim](#stmt-thm-gradient-realization) / [proof](#proof-stmt-thm-gradient-realization): Construct a bounded-rank baseline, solve the quotient response by annihilator duality, compress residual pure forms, and factor corrections through private channels. -> Abstract primal-channel prescriptions certifying the cross holes upon actual agreement.
- **step-filtered-collision** [claim](#stmt-prop-collision) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-collision): Record unary cells at fixed parameter pairs, prune tiny cells by Fubini, and Fourier-test the remaining scalar Gram entries using quotient image ranks. -> A quantitative cross-hole event retaining the required colour or type predicate.
- **step-phase-dichotomy** [claim](#stmt-thm-phase-alternative) / [proof](#proof-stmt-thm-phase-alternative): Use rank growth without covers, offset records inside large covers, and the translated-channel thinning gain inside tiny covers. -> Positive retained mass with either phase mixing or an identically zero full-sum phase.
- **step-independent-injection** [claim](#stmt-lem-injection) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-injection): Probe adaptive pin spaces with independent primal spans and compare repeated channel failures with an absolute reference-law count. -> An unconditional injection-failure bound available for subtraction.
- **step-prediction-exactification** [claim](#stmt-lem-zero-delta) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-zero-delta): Exactify small Boolean errors, compare common predictors on affine slices, and use synthetic cross-coefficient ranks to exclude unequal coefficients. -> Exact empty-status identities and equal coefficients on zero tensor-difference branches.
- **step-pooled-status-preparation** [claim](#stmt-prop-status-preparation) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-status-preparation): Retain prediction classes or the no-prediction alternative, apply phase compatibility, subtract injection failures, and trim restricted leaves without adding pins. -> Prepared positive-mass table events and a different-colour event after equal-colour subtraction.
- **step-finite-gram-comparisons** [claim](#stmt-lem-reference-product) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-reference-product): Count prescribed Gram normalizations and expand mutual and off-position Gram conditions into binary characters. -> Uniform Gram normalization, batch decoupling, and product testing under the key reference.
- **step-histogram-compactness** [claim](#stmt-lem-histogram-control) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-histogram-control): Bound many-query Fourier patterns, derive coarse entropy tails, and refine partitions until every filtered density is approximated. -> Uniform small-set control, own-leaf finite nets, and uniform integrability.
- **step-typicality-and-binary-mixing** [claim](#stmt-lem-binary-mixing) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-binary-mixing): Use paired oversampling for common-test concentration and high-rank character bounds for the specified binary constraints. -> Typical common-test integrals and weight-uniform binary mixing.
- **step-unary-key-positivity** [claim](#stmt-lem-unary-positivity) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-unary-positivity): Bound quadratic sign bias under input-coordinate transformations and apply a martingale argument on prescribed common key cells. -> Positive conditional fractions for every feasible role and basis status after summing the channel flag.
- **step-weak-product-comparison** [claim](#stmt-thm-weak-product) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-product-terminal-remainder-2): Recursively refine twisted group partitions, leave remainders terminal, and control them on actual inputs through a repeated Cauchy–Schwarz expansion. -> Global unary approximants with reference and actual-query guarantees and factorized structured integration.
- **step-global-projections** [claim](#stmt-lem-limit-global-projection) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-limit-global-projection): Average positive operators over own-leaf net representatives and quantize their significant eigenfunctions. -> Common deterministic partitions controlling adaptive cross-leaf inner products.
- **step-common-signature-limit** [claim](#stmt-lem-limit-model) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-limit-model): Close countable global test lists under projections and product approximants, and retain conditional laws as compact coordinates before taking subsequences. -> A common model with dominated status densities, independent unary reference projections, and preserved table events.
- **step-zero-product-and-density** [claim](#stmt-prop-limit-overlap) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-limit-overlap): Pass truncated overlaps through common projections, remove truncation by uniform integrability, and identify full successful densities using both product comparisons. -> An obstruction to passed usable options with positive overlap at every matched position.
- **step-scalar-duality-and-prediction** [claim](#stmt-lem-status-span) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-status-span): Dualize the scalar constraints, extract common predictors from persistent obstructions, and use prepared prediction classes to annihilate dual target evaluations. -> Robust scalar solvability on positive passed-table mass.
- **step-fresh-lists-and-overlap** [claim](#stmt-prop-positive-overlap) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-positive-overlap): Stabilize generator spans under label deletion, correct generic lifts with short kernel words, and refine positive overlaps into full numerical options. -> A fixed permitted numerical option with positive subsequential expected overlap.
- **step-coloured-distribution** [claim](#stmt-prop-coloured-distribution) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-coloured-distribution): Subtract equal-colour original pair mass before selecting numerical options, then apply positive overlap and filtered collision. -> The different-colour unit conflict distribution test.
- **step-point-side-prediction-exclusion** [claim](#stmt-lem-asym-no-point-prediction) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-asym-no-point-prediction): Compute channel character correlations on common keys and compare independently successful frames against a fixed alleged common predictor. -> Absence of a point-side prediction on any fixed positive limiting mass.
- **step-asymmetric-distribution** [claim](#stmt-prop-asymmetric-distribution) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-asymmetric-distribution): Prepare only an empty prediction if present, obtain independent-point phase compatibility, encode candidate tables by separate flags, and solve the mixed dual system. -> The unit–point conflict distribution test.
- **step-entropy-terminal-covers** [claim](#stmt-gt-flow-cut) / [proof](#proof-stmt-gt-flow-cut): Use constrained entropy variation, nonnegative resource-price separation, and a capacitated residual cut. -> Entropy deletion increments and small-capacity coloured and uncoloured infeasibility covers.
- **step-terminal-fingerprints** [claim](#stmt-gt-fingerprints) / [proof](#proof-stmt-gt-fingerprints): Record deterministic maximal-neighbourhood choices and charge every successful recording to a constrained entropy increase. -> Subexponentially many replayable terminal containers.
- **step-finite-base-graphs** [claim](#stmt-item-base-holes) / [proof](#pm-h-85): Sample positions independently, merge matching classes into a fixed palette, and union-bound terminal position and disjoint-pair exceptions. -> A finite graph sample satisfying all base conflict properties and bounded independence number.
- **step-main-and-colouring-corollaries** [claim](#stmt-thm-main) / [proof](#pm-h-5): Fix a base graph before growing its clique blow-up, apply the matrix obstruction and rank-nullity, and combine independent-set colouring estimates. -> The chromatic counterexamples, their fractional strengthening, and the linear list-colouring upper bound.
- **step-compact-measures** [claim](#stmt-lem-compact-measures) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-compact-measures): Use nested finite partitions, interval subdivision, and diagonal coordinate subsequences. -> Weak compactness of measures and compactness of countable arrays.
- **step-cylinder-densities** [claim](#stmt-lem-cylinder-densities) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-cylinder-densities): Take mean-square limits of consistent finite-prefix conditional density averages and extend cylinder identities to Borel sets. -> Jointly measurable densities and convergence of finite-prefix conditional averages.

For all sufficiently large $n$ there are subsets $A_e^\\pm\\subseteq V_e^\\pm$, each of density $(1+o(1))2^{-\\rho N}$, with the following properties. Keep the ${\\mathsf P_0}$-marginal on all primal frames $(P_e,Q_e)_e$. Given those frames, condition the original channel law on $$\\label{eq:channel-allowed}\n X_e c\\in A_e^+,\\qquad Y_e c\\in A_e^-\n \\quad(e\\in\\mathcal E, 0\\ne c\\in\\mathbb F_2^h).$$ This conditional event has positive probability for every primal frame. The resulting probability law $\\pi$ satisfies:*\n\n1.  *Its primal marginal is exactly that of ${\\mathsf P_0}$, and $$\\label{eq:thinning-density}\n     \\pi^2\\le 2^{\\varepsilon_{\\rm ch}N}{\\mathsf P_0}^2.$$*\n\n2.  *For every fixed independent ambient $q$-tuple, $q\\le q_{\\rm test}$, transpose evaluation by any specified channel frame has failure probability at most $2^{q-h+1}+o(1)$ under $\\pi$, uniformly in the tuple. More generally every fixed finite union of these rank-failure tests has its ${\\mathsf P_0}$-probability plus $o(1)$ as an upper bound.*\n\n3.  *Given any primal frames, any component and sign, and any nonzero $v\\in V_e^\\pm$, $$\\label{eq:channel-translate}\n     \\pi\\bigl\\{\\exists c\\ne0:\\ X_ec\\in A_e^++v\n                  \\mid(P,Q)\\bigr\\}\\le2^{-\\rho N/2},$$ with the analogous statement for $Y_e,A_e^-$.*\n\n*The error in <span class=\"upright\">(b)</span> is exponentially small in $N$. The ambient tuple there is fixed before sampling the vertex; no uniform conditional rank bound for a tuple selected from the sampled primal frame is asserted.",
          "source_id": "PM-157.2"
        }

          "anchor": "stmt-prop-status-preparation",
          "exact_quote": "There are constants $\\delta_*,c_*>0$, fixed before the selector and channel sizes, with the following property. Along a subsequence, the original pooled unit law has a restriction of mass at least $\\delta_*$ whose first pin dimension is at most $K_1$ and whose normalized leaves satisfy [eq:final-leaf-minentropy](#eq:final-leaf-minentropy). One of the following descriptions applies.*\n\n1.  *There is no prediction as in [def:prediction](#def:prediction) on the first pooled law before the final negligible leaf trimming. For independent draws from the prepared law, the probability of an admissible injecting actual small table is greater than $.99$.*\n\n2.  *A prediction with fixed $\\alpha_i,c$ and common classes $e_i$ is retained. Its marks and exceptions are preserved, and [eq:prediction](#eq:prediction) has uniform $o(1)$ error on every retained unit. If both classes vanish, [eq:exact-prediction](#eq:exact-prediction) is exact on every unit. For independent draws from the prepared law, the probability of an admissible injecting actual table satisfying [eq:phase-compatibility](#eq:phase-compatibility) is at least $1/64$.*\n\n\n*In particular the corresponding successful pair event, measured in two draws from the original pooled law, has mass at least $c_*$. One may take $$\\delta_* = \\frac{10^{-6}\\delta_{\\mathrm{ph}}}{64},\n \\qquad c_* = \\frac{\\delta_*^2}{64},\n \\qquad 0<\\eta_{\\mathrm{col}}<\\frac{c_*}{4},\n \\label{eq:preparation-early-margins}$$ where $0<\\delta_{\\mathrm{ph}}\\le1$ is the early retained-mass constant in [thm:phase-alternative](#thm:phase-alternative). The colour bound in [eq:preparation-early-margins](#eq:preparation-early-margins) can be chosen using the initial $M$ and early geometric constants only; the marginal constant $L$ of the second distribution test does not enter it.*\n\n*After forgetting colour and other marks, the prepared law $\\sigma'$ satisfies $$\\sigma'_i\\le\\frac{M}{\\delta_*}\\pi\\quad(i=1,2),\n \\qquad\n \\sigma'\\le 2^{(D+o(1))N}{\\mathsf P_0}^2.\n \\label{eq:prepared-marginals}$$ The endpoint primal marginals consequently have the same constant bound relative to $\\operatorname{pr}_*{\\mathsf P_0}$. Every normalized leaf has joint density at most $2^{O(N)}{\\mathsf P_0}^2$. The successful table event is detected by a finite list of numerical tables and separate unary orientation flags, together with leaf-pair tests. The size of this list is fixed in $n$, but need not be early.",

          "anchor": "stmt-lem-histogram-gram-normalization",
          "exact_quote": "Let $a$ plus slots and $b$ minus slots in one ambient component be independent uniform vectors, and prescribe their entire $a$ by $b$ Gram matrix. If $a+b\\le N/2$, the probability of that prescription together with injectivity in each mode is $$2^{-ab}\\bigl(1+O(2^{-N+a+b})\\bigr),$$ uniformly in the prescribed matrix. The same statement holds for a fixed collection of independent endpoint/component groups, with the sum of their Gram-bit counts in place of $ab$ and a fixed factor in the error bound. In particular, for a bounded number of slots all relevant Gram normalizations and their ratios are bounded above and below by positive constants, uniformly in the nominal inputs.",
          "source_id": "PM-157.2"
        },
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-lem-histogram-batch-comparison",
          "exact_quote": "Consider two bounded batches of prescribed nominal columns in one raw endpoint, or in two independent raw endpoints. Suppose their union is nominally independent in every endpoint, component, and mode. Let $F$ and $G$ be bounded functions of the separate image batches, respectively. The difference between their joint raw expectation and the product of their separate raw expectations is $$O\\bigl(\\lVert F\\rVert_\\infty\\lVert G\\rVert_\\infty 2^{-N/2}\\bigr).$$ The bound is uniform in the independent nominal columns and all their prescribed same-endpoint Gram entries. The functions may also depend on the fixed nominal inputs determining their own batch.",
          "source_id": "PM-157.2"
        },
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-lem-reference-product",
          "exact_quote": "For a fixed query shape and arbitrary global single-key functions $f_{j,n}$ with $\\lvert f_{j,n}\\rvert\\le1$, $$\\int\\prod_jf_{j,n}(k_j)\\,d\\nu_n\n =\\prod_j\\int f_{j,n}\\,d\\Omega_{l_j,q_j,n}\n   +O(2^{-N/2}).$$ The bound is uniform over the functions.",
          "source_id": "PM-157.2"
        }
      ],

          "anchor": "stmt-lem-histogram-many-queries",
          "exact_quote": "Fix a bounded query shape. There are constants $c_1,c_2>0$, independent of any key-space partition, with the following property. Put $\\ell=\\lfloor c_1n\\rfloor$ and repeat the query independently $\\ell$ times at a common orientation. Let $A_1,\\ldots,A_\\ell$ be cells of a partition of the full slot space, with weights $w_j=\\omega_n(A_j)$. Suppose the partition has bounded size and its nonempty weights have a positive lower bound along the sequence under consideration. Conditional on any nominal inputs whose queried columns are jointly independent in every endpoint, component, and mode, the raw image probability that each query $j$ lies in $A_j$ is at most $$\\label{eq:histogram-many-query-bound}\n 2^{c_2\\ell}\\prod_{j=1}^{\\ell}w_j$$ for all sufficiently large $n$. How large $n$ must be may depend on the partition and its weight bound. The constants $c_1,c_2$ do not.*\n\n*The probability, over the repeated fresh parameters, that the required nominal independence fails tends to zero exponentially in $n$, uniformly over the common orientation.",
          "source_id": "PM-157.2"
        },
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-lem-histogram-control",
          "exact_quote": "Fix a query shape, a constant $C_L$, and an integer $F$. The net itself may depend on the leaf.*\n\n3.  *Both conclusions persist after restricting the query to $\\mathcal K_n$ and expressing the subdensities relative to $\\nu_n$.           "anchor": "stmt-lem-typicality",
          "exact_quote": "Let $F_n$ be a uniformly bounded common function of the inputs and primal keys of a fixed bounded query, with no other orientation dependence. In particular it does not inspect channel maps or the orientation’s marks. Put $$A_n(O)=\\mathbb E_z F_n(z,K(O,z)),\\qquad\n m_n=\\mathbb E_{O\\sim{\\mathsf P_0}^2,z}F_n(z,K(O,z)).$$ For every fixed $\\varepsilon>0$, under <a href=\"#eq:histogram-mixed-caps\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:histogram-mixed-caps\">[eq:histogram-mixed-caps]</a>, $$\\rho_n\\{\\lvert A_n-m_n\\rvert>\\varepsilon\\}=2^{-\\Omega(n)}.$$ Repeated labels in the query are allowed. The constants may depend on the query and $\\varepsilon$, but the estimate is uniform over tests with the given sup bound. The exceptional set may depend on the test.*\n\n*For a query at just one endpoint, its raw variance about its raw mean is $2^{-\\Omega(n)}$.           "anchor": "stmt-lem-histogram-quadratic-bias",
          "exact_quote": "Let $Q$ be a quadratic function on a binary vector space and let its polar form have rank $2r$. Its uniform sign bias has magnitude at most $2^{-r}$.         },
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-lem-unary-positivity",
          "exact_quote": "Fix an endpoint, tag, label, flavor, and feasible tester summary with diagonal $q$. For a bounded number of common global key tests, its empirical conditional key frequencies differ from $\\Omega_{l,q,n}$ by any prescribed fixed tolerance except on exponentially small mixed mass under <a href=\"#eq:histogram-mixed-caps\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:histogram-mixed-caps\">[eq:histogram-mixed-caps]</a>.*\n\n*At each unit, let $C_i\\subset\\mathcal X$ be any orientation-dependent space of dimension at most $K^2$ all of whose elements have total component rank at most $K$, and choose any basis. Fix a sequence of global single-key sets $A_n$ with $\\Omega_{l,q,n}(A_n)\\ge\\delta>0$. Except on exponentially small mixed mass, every basis assignment has, conditional on the tester summary and on $K_i\\in A_n$, fraction at least $(7/8)2^{-\\dim C_i}$. For the fixed common key sets, the exceptional event depends only on the primal frames and is chosen uniformly over all nominal profiles of the indicated rank before $C_i$ or its basis is selected. Thus these selections may depend on the channels and all orientation marks. We use the first effective spaces from <a href=\"#eq:effective-space\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:effective-space\">[eq:effective-space]</a>; the larger generality in this statement requires no further peeling.*\n\n\n*For the full generic flavor and inputs conditional just on $q$, the following conservative constant is valid: $$\\label{eq:uniform-base-fraction}\n \\beta_{\\mathrm{base}}=2^{-K^2-1}4^{-(g^2+1)}>0.$$ For every feasible specified tester summary and basis assignment, outside an exponentially small exceptional set, $$\\label{eq:histogram-base-cell-lower}\n \\mathbb P_z\\{K_i\\in A_n,\\ \\text{the specified summary and basis bits}\\mid q\\}\n \\ge\\beta_{\\mathrm{base}}\\,\\Omega_{l,q,n}(A_n).$$ In particular each joint choice of the role $a(\\operatorname{atom})$ and the basis bits has this lower bound, after choosing a compatible summary. Both roles are available for either possible generic $q$. No prescribed value of the channel flag $p_i$ is included in these lower bounds. If that bit is recorded together with the role and basis bits, the bound holds only after summing over its two values.*\n\n*The lower constants do not depend on $\\delta$, on the key tests, or on the orientation-dependent choice of $C_i$. The onset of the asymptotics and the exceptional-set constants may depend on a fixed positive lower bound $\\delta$.           "anchor": "stmt-thm-weak-product",
          "exact_quote": "Let $W_n$ be any sequence of real functions on $\\mathcal K_n$ with $\\lVert W_n\\rVert_\\infty\\le B$, where $B$ is fixed. Extend it to the product of the single-key spaces with the same bound. For every $\\varepsilon>0$ there are constants $L,C<\\infty$, independent of $n$, and functions $$\\label{eq:weak-product-approximant}\n S_n(k_1,\\ldots,k_r)\n   =\\sum_{a=1}^{L}c_{a,n}\\prod_{j=1}^{r}f_{a,j,n}(k_j),\n \\qquad\n \\lvert c_{a,n}\\rvert\\le C,\\quad \\lvert f_{a,j,n}\\rvert\\le1,$$ with the following properties.*\n\n\n1.  *For arbitrary global unary functions $g_{j,n}$ of bound one, $$\\label{eq:weak-product-reference}\n     \\lvert \\int(W_n-S_n)\\prod_jg_{j,n}(k_j)\\,d\\nu_n\\rvert\\le\\varepsilon$$ for all sufficiently large $n$.*\n\n\n2.  *Under any mixed unit law satisfying <a href=\"#eq:histogram-mixed-caps\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:histogram-mixed-caps\">[eq:histogram-mixed-caps]</a>, outside an exponentially small exceptional set of orientations, $$\\label{eq:weak-product-actual}\n     \\sup_{\\lvert w_j\\rvert\\le1}\n     \\lvert \\mathbb E_z\\mathcal A_n(O,z)\n           (W_n-S_n)(K(O,z))\\prod_jw_j(O,z_j)\\rvert\\le\\varepsilon.$$ The unary input weights may depend on the entire fixed orientation and on any additional marks fixed with it. The exceptional set is independent of these weights. Thus one may prescribe channel flags such as $p_i$ in a unary weight without making them common key tests or asserting positivity for their individual values.*\n\n*The functions $f_{a,j,n}$ are global key functions; they can be chosen to be indicators of sets, or finite linear combinations of such indicators with uniformly bounded complexity. They do not depend on the sampled orientation. The constants may depend on $B,\\varepsilon$ and the fixed template and construction parameters, but not on $n$.*\n\n*An additional orientation-only filter of bound one may multiply <a href=\"#eq:weak-product-actual\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:weak-product-actual\">[eq:weak-product-actual]</a> without changing it. In particular, after averaging normalized leaves, the same error control applies to unnormalized admissibility-filtered query measures, even when the filter is chosen using the opposite leaf. No assertion is made for an arbitrary additional joint input filter. For distinct marked laws, use their fixed-weight mixture, with caps checked after forgetting the marks. A retained ordered type pair or different-colour condition is an orientation/leaf-pair filter, so the same conclusion applies before normalization. All leaf averages use their actual weights; no marginal hypothesis on a separately normalized colour class is needed.",
          "source_id": "PM-157.2"
        },

          "anchor": "stmt-lem-product-twisted-regularity",
          "exact_quote": "Let $\\lvert W\\rvert\\le B$ on the product key space of $I\\cup J$, and let $\\delta>0$. The number $L'$ is bounded in terms of $B,\\delta$ and the twist count only. The functions $f_a,g_a$ may be chosen as indicators of cells in finite group partitions.",
          "source_id": "PM-157.2"
        },
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-lem-product-terminal-remainder",
          "exact_quote": "Let $I,J$ be a nontrivial partition of some of the template positions. Let $D_n$ be a common function of their global keys with $\\lVert D_n\\rVert_\\infty\\le B_1$ and $\\lVert D_n\\rVert_{\\square,\\mathcal T}\\le\\delta$. Let $\\psi_n(I,J)$ be any product of the specified nominal $L,R$ signs and global Gram signs crossing from $I$ to $J$, evaluated on their actual inputs and keys. For each fixed $\\varepsilon_{\\mathrm{emp}}>0$, except on exponentially small mixed mass, $$\\label{eq:product-remainder-actual}\n \\sup_{\\lvert f\\rvert,\\lvert g\\rvert\\le1}\n \\lvert \\mathbb E_{z_I,z_J}D_n(K_I,K_J)\\psi_n(I,J)f(O,z_I)g(O,z_J)\\rvert\n \\le\\bigl(C_3\\delta+\\varepsilon_{\\mathrm{emp}}+o(1)\\bigr)^{1/4}.$$ The constant $C_3$ and the vanishing error depend only on $B_1$ and the fixed template. The weights may depend arbitrarily on the fixed orientation. The exceptional set does not depend on those weights.",
          "source_id": "PM-157.2"

          "anchor": "stmt-cor-weak-product-factorized-integration",
          "exact_quote": "For the structured sum in <a href=\"#eq:weak-product-approximant\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:weak-product-approximant\">[eq:weak-product-approximant]</a> and arbitrary bounded unary input weights, outside exponentially small mixed mass, $$\\begin{aligned}\n\\label{eq:weak-product-factorized-integration}\n &\\mathbb E_z\\mathcal A_n(O,z)S_n(K(O,z))\\prod_jw_j(O,z_j)\\notag\\\\\n &\\qquad=\n \\kappa\\sum_{a=1}^{L}c_{a,n}\n       \\prod_j\\mathbb E_{z_j}\n        \\bigl[f_{a,j,n}(K_j(O,z_j))w_j(O,z_j)\\bigr]+o(1).\n\\end{aligned}$$ The error is uniform over the unary weights. An orientation-only filter may be included before averaging this identity over leaves. In particular the same statement applies to marked mixtures and retained type/colour pairs as in [thm:weak-product](#thm:weak-product).",
          "source_id": "PM-157.2"

        {
          "anchor": "stmt-lem-limit-global-projection",
          "exact_quote": "Let $(K_n,\\nu_n)$ be finite probability spaces. On each first-side leaf $L$ and each second-side leaf $L'$ let there be a family of subdensities. Assume that, for each fixed $R<\\infty$ and $\\varepsilon>0$, their truncations at height $R$ have $L^1(\\nu_n)$ nets of uniformly bounded size, with the nets chosen using their own leaf only. The bounds may depend on $R,\\varepsilon$ but not on $n$ or the leaf.*\n\n\n*For every $R<\\infty$ and $\\eta>0$, there are deterministic partitions $\\mathcal P_n$ of uniformly bounded size such that the following holds. These partitions may depend on the leaf laws, but are chosen before the leaves are sampled. For independent leaves, choose a member $f$ and a member $g$ of the two truncated families, allowing either choice to depend on both leaves. If $P_n$ is conditional expectation onto $\\mathcal P_n$, then $$\\label{eq:limit-projection-error}\n\\mathbb E\\bigl|\\langle f,g\\rangle-\\langle P_nf,P_ng\\rangle\\bigr|\\le\\eta.$$ The same conclusion holds for every deterministic refinement of $\\mathcal P_n$ chosen independently of the sampled leaves.       "claim_anchor": "stmt-lem-limit-model",
      "depends_on": [
        "step-global-projections",

        "step-unary-key-positivity",

      "evidence": [
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-lem-limit-model",
          "exact_quote": "There is a subsequence and a common limiting experiment with the following properties.*\n\n1.  *For each tag and diagonal bit $(l,q)$ there is a compact bit-sequence space $\\Xi_{l,q}$ with reference law $m_{l,q}$. For each key shape there is a compact tuple-test space $\\Upsilon$ with reference law $\\rho$. Here $\\rho$ denotes this measure, distinct from the scalar thinning parameter in [lem:channel-thinning](#lem:channel-thinning). Its single-position projections $\\xi_\\ell$ have the independent laws $m_{l_\\ell,q_\\ell}$.*\n\n\n2.  *A base orientation array $\\theta$ contains its bounded discrete metadata and its single-atom status measures. For a unary type $t=(i,l,s,\\varphi,q)$ and a full numerical status $\\upsilon$, these measures have jointly measurable densities $$\\label{eq:limit-unary-densities}\n    h^\\theta_{t,\\upsilon}:\\Xi_{l,q}\\longrightarrow[0,1],\\qquad\n    \\sum_\\upsilon h^\\theta_{t,\\upsilon}=1\\quad m_{l,q}\\text{-almost everywhere}.$$ For the full generic flavor, the sum of these densities over statuses with any specified role and basis vector in the recorded actual dimension is bounded below by a positive construction constant, almost everywhere. Compatible finer tester requirements have the lower fractions supplied by [lem:unary-positivity](#lem:unary-positivity).*\n\n3.  *There is first a random limiting leaf-pair record $Z$, which includes two conditional laws $\\Lambda_A,\\Lambda_B$ of the arrays and their finite flag vectors. Conditional on $Z$, the two orientation records are drawn independently from these laws. After flags are dropped and $Z$ is averaged out, $\\theta_A,\\theta_B$ are independent with their respective base laws; they are identically distributed when the two original laws coincide.
